business_problem: TCL Photovoltaic Technology's growth created more dispersed projects, more complex operating processes, and higher policy risk, so the company needed AI to improve efficiency, consistency, and control as it scaled.
solution_summary: TCL Photovoltaic Technology worked with Bain to make AI a core operating capability rather than a series of disconnected pilots. The company prioritized pain points that would block scalable growth and then introduced several implemented AI workflows. Intelligent inspection reduced reliance on manual judgment during site surveys and final grid connection reviews. A real-time analysis and forecasting capability processed power-market conditions so planners could make faster, more accurate decisions. AI-powered recognition continuously monitored power stations and flagged potential faults early, improving maintenance response speed and accuracy. Bain also helped the company stand up a dedicated AI service group so the use cases could be scaled across the business with stronger discipline and risk control. The source does not identify named storage systems, but it clearly describes a pipeline from operational and market inputs to inspection, forecasting, and station-monitoring decisions.

data_flow: Project inspection inputs, power-market signals, and operating data from power stations feed into intelligent inspection, market forecasting, and AI-powered recognition workflows. Those systems return audit decisions, forecasts, and fault alerts to business and maintenance teams, while the AI service group scales the operating model across the company.
business_outcome: TCL PV Tech reduced audit costs, improved maintenance response quality, and built an AI operating model that supports efficient scale growth while keeping risk control central to the business.
